review: 2:2–2:4 בַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא אֲהֵבָנוּ … נִצְלַב בַּעֲדֵנוּ — Galatians 2:20 (אֲשֶׁר אָהַב אֹתִי) with Eph 5:2; the Arabic ذَاكَ الَّذِي أَحَبَّنَا … قَدْ صُلِبَ لِأَجْلِنَا is that pair, and the Hebrew keeps the relative clause so the cross is the proof of the love, not a separate statement.

4:4 שֶׁמֶן תּוּרַק יָקָר — Song of Songs 1:3 (שֶׁמֶן תּוּרַק שְׁמֶךָ) and the glossary form; the Arabic الطِّيبَ الثَّمِين is 'the precious perfume', and the Hebrew keeps the Song's poured oil because the stanza is an offering of praise.

3:1–3:4 הוֹשַׁעְתָּנוּ … טִהַרְתָּנוּ, הִצְדַּקְתָּנוּ … וּבֵרַכְתָּ — 1 Cor 6:11 (טָהַרְתֶּם, הִצְדַּקְתֶּם) with Eph 1:3; the Arabic خَلَّصْتَنَا / طَهَّرْتَنَا بَرَّرْتَنَا is that chain, and the Hebrew keeps all four verbs in the same order and person.

1:3 נִתְאַחֵד בְּקוֹל אֶחָד — the Arabic تَتَّحِدُ أَصْوَاتُنَا is 'our voices unite'; the Hebrew reverses the image (we unite in one voice) because אֶחָד carries the unity the stanza is asking for, but the sense is unchanged.
4:2 נִכְרְעָה בְּהִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָה — the Arabic نَجْثُو سَاجِدِين is 'kneeling in worship'; כָּרַע and הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה are the two biblical verbs of bowing (Ps 95:6), kept as a pair.
